title: Marlowe & Finch Registrant Terms — Registry Price Protection on Merchandise Purchases
content:
**Who may claim.** A registrant who bought an item that is listed on her own gift registry, and whose registry afterwards records a guest gift of the identical item (same item number) at a lower net price within the class's price-adjustment window, may claim registry price protection on that Merchandise Purchases unit.

**How the claim is made.** The claim is the registrant's own act: she files it in person through the price protection claim on her order, with the amount this rule gives, as a price-drop adjustment refunded to the unit's original tender, and the new unit price recorded on it is the protection lower price.

**Scope of the claim.**
- For a registry price protection claim this policy handles, and only for such a claim, the refund is the protected difference, capped, plus the sales tax on it, plus the registrant goodwill amounts, paid to the unit's original tender and never as a gift card; every other price-drop adjustment remains under the base rule.
- For a registry price protection claim this policy handles, and only for such a claim, the unit's earlier price-drop adjustments still number fewer than the class's per-unit limit, and the protection difference, measured from the protection base price rather than from the latest adjustment entry, is at least the class's smallest refundable difference; every other price-drop adjustment remains under the base rule.
- For a registry price protection claim this policy handles, and only for such a claim, the unit is in completed status, received by the registrant and not put into return; every other price adjustment keeps the base status condition.

**When the refund is fixed.**
- The registry price protection refund on a unit is fixed only after the unit's records carry a register-error correction to its shelf ticket price for any amount the unit was rung above that ticket.
- The registry price protection refund is not worked out until the unit's records carry a register-error correction recording no new unit price for any registry credit spent on the unit and left undeducted.

## Conditions of a claim at a glance

| Condition | Read from |
|---|---|
| the item is listed on the registrant's own registry and she bought it | the registry and the purchase record |
| a guest gift of the same item number at a lower net price is recorded afterwards, within the class's price-adjustment window | the registry's guest gift entries |
| the unit is completed, received by the registrant and not put into return | the purchase record |
| earlier price-drop adjustments number fewer than the class's per-unit limit | the unit's adjustment entries |
| the protection difference is at least the class's smallest refundable difference | the unit's records |

## Handing the claim to the registrant — `claim_registry_price_protection_38d04d45`

**Capability.** Files a registry price protection claim on one of the registrant's own purchases: the registrant claims the price protection on an item from her own gift registry that a guest later bought at a lower price, stating that lower price and the protection amount the representative gave her. On success one price-drop adjustment entry with the current date, the lower price recorded as the new unit price on that entry and the amount is added to the purchase; the amount is refunded to the tender the registrant paid with, and the purchase's amount paid and not refunded goes down by the same amount. The selling price on the purchase record is left as charged. The registrant sees the refund on her original tender.

**How it is invoked.** `claim_registry_price_protection_38d04d45` is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `purchase_id` | the reference number of the registrant's purchase record (one unit of one item) the claim is for, as read to her by the representative from the purchase lookup | identifier text |
| `new_unit_price` | the lower price the protection is based on, recorded as the new unit price on the price-drop adjustment entry | USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent; never empty |
| `amount` | the protection amount refunded, as the representative gave it to her | USD, 2 decimal places, positive, rounded half up to the cent; never empty |

No parameter takes an enumerated value.

**Return.** A confirmation sentence naming the new price adjustment reference number (an opaque text reference), the purchase record reference number, the protection lower price and the amount refunded (both USD with 2 decimal places), the tender refunded, and the purchase's remaining amount paid and not refunded (USD, 2 decimal places). A sentence starting with "Registry price protection claim filed" means the claim was recorded.
